When a view needs to pause and resume without losing state (e.g. keeping an open conversation alive while a backend reconnects), prefer hiding it with React's `<Activity>` instead of conditionally unmounting it. Hidden `Activity` content keeps component state but tears down effects, which is exactly what releases focus traps, portaled dialogs, and `body` pointer-events locks that a simple CSS-hide or "cover with an overlay" approach would leave dangling.

This pattern only works if every effect's cleanup is written to be safe for a hide, not just a true unmount:

- Any mutable ref driving a scheduler (a flush timer, a reconcile timer) must be reset to its "idle" value (e.g. `timerRef.current = null`) inside the cleanup, not just have its timeout cleared. Otherwise, when the view is shown again, the scheduling function sees a stale non-null ref, assumes a timer is already armed, and silently drops future work.
- Any transient UI flag backed by external async state (a recording/listening flag, a loading flag) must be reset in the same cleanup that cancels the underlying operation, so the corresponding "went inactive" callback fires again once the view reappears.
- An effect meant to run its side effect only once per lifetime (e.g. an initial navigation/bootstrap dispatch) must gate on a ref flag, since refs — unlike effect-run-count — survive an `Activity` hide/show cycle; plain effect dependencies will rerun that logic on every show and can stomp on user-driven state in between.

```tsx
function useSomething() {
  const timerRef = useRef<number | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    return () => {
      if (timerRef.current !== null) {
        window.clearTimeout(timerRef.current);
        timerRef.current = null; // not just cleared — reset so re-show re-arms it
      }
    };
  }, []);
}

function useBootstrapOnce() {
  const bootstrappedRef = useRef(false); // survives Activity hide
  useEffect(() => {
    void loadContext().then((result) => {
      refreshDerivedState(result); // safe to repeat on every show
      if (!bootstrappedRef.current) {
        bootstrappedRef.current = true;
        dispatchInitialNavigation(result); // only once, ever
      }
    });
  }, []);
}
```

Before shipping any hide/show (or similar remount-avoiding) lifecycle change, write a test that mounts the component, toggles it hidden and visible again mid-operation, and asserts the in-flight work (pending stream flush, active recording, queued navigation) still completes or resumes correctly — unmount-only cleanup bugs are invisible until that exact sequence is exercised.
